rows.text: Urza turns every artifact you control into a blue mana. Not artifacts that tap for mana — ALL of them: the Construct token he brings with him, Clues, Baubles, Equipment, even Sol Ring after you have already tapped it for its own mana would not work, but everything untapped does. That one line is why this deck's mana is effectively its board, and why an untap effect is the same thing as a ritual.

rows.name: Urza, Lord High Artificer
rows.text: arrives with a Construct that is as big as your artifact count, taps any untapped artifact for {U}, and his {5} ability exiles the top card of your library and lets you play it free.
Tapping an artifact for Urza's mana uses it up. You cannot tap Sol Ring for {C}{C} and then tap it again for Urza — pick one. That is the main thing people get wrong.
The {5} ability is the deck's engine once mana is unlimited: shuffle, exile, cast free, repeat until you find the kill.

rows.name: Isochron Scepter

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep cheap artifacts and a land. Mox Opal, Lotus Petal, Mishra's Bauble and Sol Ring all make Urza a turn-three play and immediately turn into mana once he lands.
Count Urza's mana correctly. Each untapped artifact is one blue, once. Tapping Sol Ring for its own two means it is no longer available for Urza — work out which use you need before you start.

rows.name: Muddle the Mixture
rows.text: remember it transmutes for exactly two. Isochron Scepter, Basalt Monolith and Power Artifact are all two, so it is a tutor for whichever combo half you are missing.
Hold up interaction on the turn you go off. The deck's failure case is a single counterspell on Dramatic Reversal, and Force of Negation or Pact of Negation costs you nothing to keep available.
